answer: Stop sybils with an oasis, a fable, and a thread. The oasis admits only one new identity per beacon pulse, so slots stay scarce. Each applicant must carry a fable: a unique personal-history attestation, checked for near-duplicates, so a copied fable voids both copies. Admitted identities join one thread: each newcomer is vouched by a member, and if any member cheats, the whole thread is slashed together. Cloning N identities on one thread risks losing all N bonds at once, while splitting them needs N distinct fable texts and N scarce oasis slots, so attack cost grows faster than N.
